name: Palti
overview: Palti was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily for being one of the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan. His role as a spy is recorded in Numbers 13:9, highlighting his participation in this significant event during Israel's wilderness journey.
namesAndTitles: The name Palti means 'G-d is my deliverance,' reflecting a declaration of trust in God's saving power. This proper name, though not given directly by God, conveys a meaningful attribute associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Palti is identified as the son of Raphu, establishing a clear familial link recorded in Scripture. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Palti's significance lies in his selection as one of the twelve spies representing the tribe of Benjamin, entrusted with scouting the Promised Land. This role placed him at a pivotal moment in Israel's history, as the spies' report influenced the nation's faith and obedience to God's promise. His inclusion among the spies underscores his standing within the tribe and the community during this formative period.
